html:
Bia Mbyá is a self-name of the Yuqui, a small Tupi-Guarani-speaking people of the Chapare forest in Cochabamba, Bolivia. They are close relatives of the Sirionó.

The Yuqui lived as nomadic hunters and gatherers in small bands, avoiding outsiders. Missionaries of the New Tribes Mission made peaceful contact with them between the 1960s and 1980s and gathered them at a station on the Chimoré River. Their numbers had fallen to a few dozen, and disease and the spread of coca farming and settlers in the Chapare have kept them under pressure. Their neighbours include the Yuracaré.
